newsitem.title: UK: UK grain futures down on European prices, currency.
newsitem.headline: UK grain futures down on European prices, currency.

text.p: LIFFE wheat futures fell on weak continental prices and currency factors, traders said.

Danish price falls in particular, coupled with the strength of sterling, helped prices down during the morning, while later in the day the announcement of a UK green rate revaluation, due to take effect from Tuesday, helped push prices down.

The green rate revaluation will affect the UK feed wheat market indirectly, by cutting the value in sterling terms of the intervention price paid for milling quality wheat. "It should take five pounds off the intervention price," was one London trader's first estimate of the effect.

Sterling's green rate in the European Union's agrimonetary system will be revalued to 0.768177 per ECU with effect from Tuesday, compared with the current rate of 0.809915, the UK's Home Grown Cereals Authority said.
However, the futures market was underpinned by profit taking towards the close, traders said.
Active May wheat last traded at 94.75 stg per tonne, down 0.95 stg, on volume of 235 lots. Total wheat volume was 511 lots.
There were no trades in barley.
